input_signals.name: Durable Margin Sales Value
input_signals.hypothesis: Low price-to-sales firms outperform when their sales carry high, persistent gross margins rather than weak or unstable economics.
input_signals.reasoning: The numerator rewards average gross margin and penalizes margin volatility, while the denominator measures the market price paid per unit of sales. Industry ranking makes the quality-adjusted sales valuation comparable among firms with similar production economics.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( ma( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 3 ), vol( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 5 ) ), ratio( mul( prcc_f, csho ), sale ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Retained Profit Accumulation Yield
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms priced cheaply relative to their sustained accumulation of internally generated equity earn stronger subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The signal replaces the static retained-earnings sign screen with a continuous flow measure of additions to retained capital, normalized directly by market value. Averaging changes over three periods reduces one-year accounting noise while distinguishing internal compounders from firms consuming accumulated equity.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( ratio( ma( delta( re, 1 ), 3 ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Self-Financed EBITDA Value
input_signals.hypothesis: Debt-inclusive EBITDA bargains outperform when operating earnings are not accompanied by growth in total liabilities.
input_signals.reasoning: Liability accumulation is subtracted from smoothed EBITDA, penalizing firms whose apparent operating performance depends on supplier credit, accruals, acquisitions, or other new claims. Declining liabilities increase the conservative earnings numerator, identifying cheap firms that are simultaneously generating earnings and repairing their financing structure.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( ma( ebitda, 2 ), ma( delta( lt, 1 ), 2 ) ), add( mul( prcc_f, csho ), add( dltt, dlc ) ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Maintenance-Reserve Cash Yield
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms priced cheaply relative to cash flow remaining after a depreciation-based replacement reserve earn stronger subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Unadjusted operating cash flow can make capital-intensive or deteriorating firms appear deceptively cheap because depreciation is added back despite recurring replacement needs. Subtracting smoothed depreciation produces a conservative cash-earnings yield intended to separate distributable cash generation from capital-consumption value traps.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( ma( oancf, 2 ), ma( dp, 2 ) ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Earned-Cash Discount
input_signals.hypothesis: Cash-rich firms earn stronger subsequent returns when their cash balances are supported by accumulated internal profitability.
input_signals.reasoning: Cash-to-market identifies liquid-asset cheapness, while the retained-earnings share distinguishes earned cash from liquidity raised through external financing. Unlike multiplying two potentially zero-centered ranks, the nonnegative cash-yield leg scales a signed quality state, so accumulated deficits reduce rather than invert the signal.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( mul( ratio( che, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), ma( ratio( re, at ), 2 ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Through-Cycle Margin Floor Value
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms priced cheaply relative to sales outperform when even their recent worst-case gross margin indicates resilient unit economics.
input_signals.reasoning: The historical margin floor converts current sales into a conservative through-cycle gross-profit capacity rather than reproducing current gross-profits-to-market. Because sales yield is generally nonnegative, a weak or negative margin floor lowers the signal without the sign inversion created by multiplying two centered ranks.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( mul( ratio( sale, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), ts_min( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 3 ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Liquidity-Recovery Book Bargain
input_signals.hypothesis: High book-to-market firms outperform when their net liquid-asset position is improving relative to total assets.
input_signals.reasoning: Unlike the static net-net ratio, this signal uses book value for valuation and the trajectory of normalized liquidity as a separate quality state. The weak-link interaction requires both a genuine book discount and balance-sheet recovery, reducing exposure to firms that remain cheap because liquidity continues to deteriorate.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( winsor( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( trend( ratio( sub( act, lt ), at ), 3 ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Working-Capital-Release-Adjusted Cash Yield
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms priced cheaply relative to operating cash flow after removing cash generated through working-capital liquidation earn stronger subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The positive-part adjustment subtracts only declines in noncash working capital that temporarily boost operating cash flow; it does not add back working-capital investment. This asymmetric treatment is conservative and avoids reconstructing the conventional cash-flow-to-price numerator.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( ratio( ma( sub( oancf, max( neg( delta( sub( sub( act, che ), lct ), 1 ) ), sub( act, act ) ) ), 2 ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Enterprise Earned-Cash Discount
input_signals.hypothesis: Cash is more likely to be undervalued when it is inexpensive relative to total capital claims and supported by accumulated internal profitability.
input_signals.reasoning: This retains enterprise scaling to reduce concentration in small, levered cash-rich firms but replaces the empirically weak operating-cash-flow-to-current-liabilities leg with the better-supported retained-earnings quality state. The cash ratio is nonnegative, so accumulated deficits intentionally reduce the score rather than creating a flow-driven sign inversion.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( mul( ratio( che, add( mul( prcc_f, csho ), add( dltt, dlc ) ) ), ma( ratio( re, at ), 2 ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Historically Restored Margin Value
input_signals.hypothesis: Low price-to-sales firms outperform when gross margins are both economically strong and near the top of the firm’s own recent history.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the generic book-value-plus-improving-profitability construction with a firm-specific margin-restoration mechanism. The nested weak-link interaction requires cheap sales, a strong margin level, and a favorable within-firm margin position, preventing any single textbook value or quality leg from dominating.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( winsor( ratio( sale, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 1 ) ), min( rank( winsor( ma( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 2 ), 1 ) ), rank( ts_rank( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Deficit-Adjusted Cash Value
input_signals.hypothesis: Cash-rich firms earn stronger subsequent returns when their cash discount is not offset by a cumulative retained-earnings deficit.
input_signals.reasoning: Unlike cash-to-price multiplied by a generic profitability rank, this construction treats accumulated losses as a stock claim against the apparent cash surplus. The asymmetric penalty leaves positive-retained-earnings firms on a normal cash-value scale while continuously demoting cash-rich firms with deep historical deficits.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( ratio( che, add( mul( prcc_f, csho ), max( neg( re ), sub( re, re ) ) ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Operating-Asset-Liquidation-Adjusted Cash Yield
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms priced cheaply relative to operating cash flow after removing proceeds from noncash current-asset liquidation earn stronger subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Declines in noncash current assets, unlike generic increases in current liabilities, represent operating working-capital releases that directly elevate operating cash flow. The one-sided haircut therefore removes an identifiable liquidation benefit without incorrectly treating short-term borrowing as an operating inflow.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( ratio( ma( sub( oancf, max( neg( delta( sub( act, che ), 1 ) ), sub( act, act ) ) ), 2 ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Bounded Operating Claim Yield
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms priced cheaply relative to conservatively cash-realizable operating earnings earn stronger subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The lower of smoothed EBITDA and operating cash flow prevents reported operating earnings from exceeding their cash realization while giving no extra reward when cash flow temporarily exceeds EBITDA. Both numerator inputs are flows and the denominator is a stock of equity and liability claims, eliminating the prior flow-stock adjustment mismatch.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( ratio( min( ma( ebitda, 2 ), ma( oancf, 2 ) ), add( mul( prcc_f, csho ), lt ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Retained-Earnings Rollforward Value
input_signals.hypothesis: High earnings-yield firms earn stronger subsequent returns when reported income reconciles with additions to retained earnings plus common dividends.
input_signals.reasoning: The retained-earnings rollforward provides an accounting-identity quality check rather than another profitability level or growth signal. Subtracting the absolute unexplained residual from earnings penalizes cheap firms affected by restatements, direct-to-equity adjustments, or other opaque reconciliation items; unreported dividends are treated as zero.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( ma( ib, 2 ), ma( abs( sub( ib, add( delta( re, 1 ), coalesce( dvc, sub( re, re ) ) ) ) ), 2 ) ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Accrual-Bounded Cash Yield
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms priced cheaply relative to the lower of operating cash flow and accrual-implied cash earnings earn stronger subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Income plus depreciation provides an accrual-based cash-earnings benchmark, while reported operating cash flow captures realized cash generation. Taking the lower value prevents temporary working-capital releases from inflating the signal without requiring the sparse current-asset-change data used by earlier liquidation adjustments.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( ratio( min( ma( oancf, 2 ), ma( add( ib, dp ), 2 ) ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Signed Deficit-Adjusted Cash Yield
input_signals.hypothesis: Positive operating cash flow predicts stronger returns when it is inexpensive and not undermined by accumulated deficits, while negative operating cash flow remains an unambiguously adverse signal.
input_signals.reasoning: The expression separates positive and negative cash-flow branches: deficits enlarge the denominator only for positive cash flow, while negative cash flow enters as an explicitly negative yield. This removes the prior sign reversal that made deficit-laden cash burners appear less negative and therefore artificially better ranked.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( sub( ratio( max( ma( oancf, 2 ), sub( re, re ) ), add( mul( prcc_f, csho ), max( neg( re ), sub( re, re ) ) ) ), ratio( max( neg( ma( oancf, 2 ) ), sub( re, re ) ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Short-Term Funding Sales Trap
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that appear inexpensive relative to sales underperform when current liabilities are rising persistently relative to the operating costs they support.
input_signals.reasoning: Current liabilities are evaluated relative to cost of goods sold rather than treated as a direct offset to cash holdings, distinguishing operating funding pressure from a static cash anomaly. The nonnegative sales-yield leg amplifies a signed deterioration in short-term funding intensity without relying on unstable operating-cash-flow coverage.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( mul( ratio( sale, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), trend( ratio( lct, cogs ), 3 ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Continuous Maintenance Sales Value
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with inexpensive sales earn stronger subsequent returns when those sales support positive maintenance-adjusted cash profitability.
input_signals.reasoning: The earlier MIN combination of these channels produced a poor long-short portfolio because any weak leg pushed heterogeneous firms into the short tail. This continuous interaction instead makes cash-burning firms explicitly negative and scales positive maintenance profitability by sales cheapness, preserving economically ordered tails.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( mul( ratio( sale, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), ma( ratio( sub( oancf, dp ), at ), 2 ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: EBITDA-Cash Concordance Claim Yield
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms priced cheaply relative to operating earnings earn stronger subsequent returns when EBITDA and operating cash flow are closely aligned.
input_signals.reasoning: The prior lower-bound claim yield penalized only cash flow below EBITDA, even though unusually high cash flow can also reflect temporary working-capital liquidation. Subtracting the absolute EBITDA-cash gap creates a symmetric realization penalty while keeping the numerator in dollar flows and the denominator in total equity and liability claims.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( ma( ebitda, 2 ), ma( abs( sub( ebitda, oancf ) ), 2 ) ), add( mul( prcc_f, csho ), lt ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Working-Asset Cash Productivity Value
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with inexpensive sales earn stronger subsequent returns when their current-asset base generates high operating cash flow.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the accumulated-deficit cash-stock construction with an operating-efficiency mechanism linking sales valuation to cash productivity. The nonnegative sales-yield leg scales a signed cash-return measure, so cash-consuming firms receive negative scores rather than benefiting from a denominator adjustment.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( mul( ratio( sale, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), ma( ratio( oancf, act ), 2 ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Productive Deficit-Adjusted Cash Value
input_signals.hypothesis: Deficit-adjusted cash bargains earn stronger subsequent returns when current-asset productivity is also improving.
input_signals.reasoning: The accumulated-deficit cash ratio supplies the strongest broad-coverage value evidence, while improving sales per current asset distinguishes productive liquidity from idle cash accumulation. Using separate ranked channels avoids sign reversals and does not mechanically multiply cash value by a potentially negative quality state.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( sumrank( winsor( ratio( che, add( mul( prcc_f, csho ), max( neg( re ), sub( re, re ) ) ) ), 1 ), winsor( trend( ratio( sale, act ), 3 ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Funding-Safe Maintenance Sales Value
input_signals.hypothesis: Maintenance-cash-supported sales bargains earn stronger returns when short-term funding pressure is easing rather than intensifying.
input_signals.reasoning: Continuous maintenance sales value generated coherent slope and portfolio evidence, while rising current liabilities relative to costs reliably identified the opposite trap tail. The ranked composite preserves both effects on comparable scales without multiplying two signed quantities or allowing worsening funding pressure to improve the score.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( sumrank( winsor( mul( ratio( sale, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), ma( ratio( sub( oancf, dp ), at ), 2 ) ), 1 ), winsor( neg( trend( ratio( lct, cogs ), 3 ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Maintenance-Productive Cash Discount
input_signals.hypothesis: Cash-rich firms earn stronger subsequent returns when ongoing operations generate positive cash profitability after a depreciation-based replacement reserve.
input_signals.reasoning: The cash-yield leg is nonnegative, so maintenance cash profitability determines the signal’s direction without sign inversion: cash-burning firms receive negative scores and productive firms positive scores. This tests whether the strong cash-discount and maintenance-cash mechanisms reinforce one another continuously rather than only through a distress-only denominator penalty.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( mul( ratio( che, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), ma( ratio( sub( oancf, dp ), at ), 2 ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Uncovered Claim Growth Trap
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms underperform when growth in current liabilities exceeds operating cash generation by a large amount relative to market value.
input_signals.reasoning: This measures a single funding-shortfall mechanism rather than averaging separate productivity and funding-pressure signals. The liability change and operating cash flow are both dollar flows, while market-value scaling makes the uncovered claim growth most consequential among apparently cheap firms.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( ratio( max( sub( delta( lct, 1 ), oancf ), sub( lct, lct ) ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Through-Cycle Depreciation-Covered EBITDA Yield
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms priced cheaply relative to EBITDA earn stronger subsequent returns when operating earnings cover a conservative through-cycle depreciation burden.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the liability-productivity substitution with a capital-consumption mechanism: recent peak depreciation serves as a conservative reserve against overstated operating earning power. Firms whose smoothed EBITDA cannot cover that reserve receive low or negative yields, reducing exposure to capital-intensive value traps.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( ma( ebitda, 2 ), ts_max( dp, 3 ) ), add( mul( prcc_f, csho ), add( dltt, dlc ) ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Covered Conservative Claim Yield
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms earn stronger subsequent returns when conservatively cash-realizable operating earnings are inexpensive relative to equity value plus liabilities not covered by cash.
input_signals.reasoning: Cash modifies the economic claim base directly rather than entering as a separately ranked value signal, while the lower-bound numerator prevents EBITDA from exceeding its cash realization. The nonnegative unfunded-liability term avoids negative-enterprise-value distortions and represents the obligations that remain after available cash coverage.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( ratio( min( ma( ebitda, 2 ), ma( oancf, 2 ) ), add( mul( prcc_f, csho ), max( sub( lt, che ), sub( lt, lt ) ) ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Funding-Safe Deficit Cash Value
input_signals.hypothesis: Deficit-adjusted cash bargains earn stronger subsequent returns when current liabilities are declining relative to the operating costs they finance.
input_signals.reasoning: Rising short-term funding intensity generated strong negative cross-sectional and portfolio evidence, making its reversal an economically supported quality state rather than an untested screen. The construction combines the cash-value level with standalone funding relief, avoiding duplication of a common price-scaled value leg.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( sumrank( winsor( ratio( che, add( mul( prcc_f, csho ), max( neg( re ), sub( re, re ) ) ) ), 1 ), winsor( neg( trend( ratio( lct, cogs ), 3 ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Liability-Origin-Adjusted Cash Value
input_signals.hypothesis: Cash-rich firms earn stronger subsequent returns when their cash balances are not explained by recent growth in liability financing.
input_signals.reasoning: This tests cash provenance rather than combining cash value with another profitability measure: positive liability growth is treated as an external source that reduces the cash plausibly generated for shareholders. The cash stock and liability change are both dollar quantities, and cash raised without liability expansion retains its full valuation weight.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( che, max( delta( lt, 1 ), sub( lt, lt ) ) ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Through-Cycle Solvency Sales Value
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms priced cheaply relative to sales earn stronger subsequent returns when current assets have consistently covered total liabilities.
input_signals.reasoning: The quality mechanism is a through-cycle uncovered-liability stock rather than another profitability or turnover trend. Because sales are generally nonnegative, adding the recent maximum solvency shortfall to the valuation denominator cannot create the sign reversal that occurs when denominator penalties are applied to negative earnings.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( ratio( ma( sale, 2 ), add( mul( prcc_f, csho ), ts_max( max( sub( lt, act ), sub( lt, lt ) ), 3 ) ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Working-Capital-Reserved Gross Profit Yield
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms priced cheaply relative to gross profit earn stronger subsequent returns when that profit does not require a large working-capital adjustment.
input_signals.reasoning: Gross profit is reduced by the absolute dollar movement in noncash operating working capital, reserving for both cash-consuming expansion and potentially temporary liquidation benefits. The construction therefore measures working-capital-realizable gross profit rather than reusing an asset-turnover trend or a standalone working-capital-growth anomaly.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( sub( sale, cogs ), abs( delta( sub( sub( act, che ), lct ), 1 ) ) ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Productive Liability-Origin Cash Value
input_signals.hypothesis: Cash balances not attributable to recent liability growth are more likely to be undervalued when current-asset productivity is improving.
input_signals.reasoning: Liability-origin-adjusted cash value produced strong evidence with broad coverage, but internally sourced cash can still be idle. The separate productivity state distinguishes cash retained by improving operations from cash associated with contraction or inefficient asset accumulation.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( sumrank( winsor( ratio( sub( che, max( delta( lt, 1 ), sub( lt, lt ) ) ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 1 ), winsor( trend( ratio( sale, act ), 3 ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Internally Earned Cash Value
input_signals.hypothesis: Cash-rich firms earn stronger subsequent returns when cash is neither offset by accumulated losses nor accompanied by recent liability expansion.
input_signals.reasoning: Accumulated deficits and positive liability growth represent distinct stock-based and financing-source encumbrances on apparent cash value. Keeping cash as a nonnegative numerator and placing both penalties in the denominator preserves sign consistency while requiring the discount to reflect plausibly internally earned liquidity.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( ratio( che, add( add( mul( prcc_f, csho ), max( neg( re ), sub( re, re ) ) ), max( delta( lt, 1 ), sub( lt, lt ) ) ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Gross-Profit Claim Coverage Value
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with inexpensive sales earn stronger subsequent returns when gross profit provides strong coverage of current liabilities.
input_signals.reasoning: This uses a single operating-coverage mechanism rather than blending previously evaluated cash and funding signals. The nonnegative sales-yield leg scales a signed gross-profit coverage measure, so firms with negative gross profit receive low scores while profitable firms with manageable near-term claims rank highly.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( mul( ratio( sale, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), ma( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), lct ), 2 ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Stable Earned-Capital Cash Value
input_signals.hypothesis: Cash-rich firms earn stronger subsequent returns when their accumulated earned-capital base is stable rather than subject to large historical revisions or swings.
input_signals.reasoning: Retained-earnings instability captures a different quality mechanism from profitability trends, accumulated deficits, or liability-funded cash provenance. Because cash and the volatility of the retained-earnings stock are both dollar stocks, the denominator treats unstable earned capital as an additional uncertainty claim on apparent cash value.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( ratio( che, add( mul( prcc_f, csho ), vol( re, 3 ) ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Creditor-for-Earned-Capital Trap
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms underperform when growth in creditor claims exceeds growth in internally earned shareholder capital by a large amount relative to market value.
input_signals.reasoning: This is a continuous capital-source substitution measure rather than another cash-coverage hinge or rank ensemble. Liability and retained-earnings changes are comparable dollar-stock flows, so a high score directly identifies cheap firms replacing earned capital with creditor financing.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( delta( lt, 1 ), delta( re, 1 ) ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 1 ) )
